clusters.state_of_play: FIFA's chief operating officer was sacked weeks after publicly accusing president Gianni Infantino of deceiving staff over a now-abandoned World Cup sell-off plan. FIFA vice president Victor Montagliani asked Infantino to stay away from a youth tournament in the Dominican Republic amid the fallout, but Infantino attended anyway. Separately, rights group FairSquare is urging FIFA to block Infantino from seeking re-election, arguing it would violate the organization's term limits. FIFA has also suspended Argentina's Leandro Paredes and other players, with fines and bans totaling 17 matches, over on-field clashes with Spain after the World Cup final. Separately, Argentina great Lionel Messi has announced his retirement from international football following Argentina's World Cup final defeat to Spain and the recent death of his father; he wrote his retirement letter after the final but delayed publishing it due to his father's health issues, revealed the decision via a social media post on Monday, and will continue playing club football for MLS side Inter Miami.
